summary: Instagram is doing the real work: almost every Hindi video gets 1,200–1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 100 views per video. The best performers are short, punchy 'X doesn't do what you think' videos about hands-on maker items like robots, clap switches, mics and PIR sensors. Generic 'how does this everyday thing know?' videos (lifts, taps, doors, smoke alarms, phones) get far fewer views, likes and saves, especially on Instagram.
winningPattern: Maker-style gadget or robot subjects (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower, mic, PIR sensor) with a surprising negative or reversal hook such as 'X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' or 'Robot would fall without this'. Hinglish titles are short, with an emoji and #shorts, and Instagram is the main driver. Videos with a visible build or demo get the most likes, saves and shares.
doMore: Make 'X doesn't do what you think' reversal hooks about Arduino-style modules and robots
Build series around the winners: clap switch, gyro robot, line follower, IR obstacle robot and mic
Show a physical demo or robot reacting in the first 2 seconds, then explain the sensor
End with a save-worthy line like 'Save this for your project' to lift saves and shares
Post to Instagram first and test YouTube-specific titles with searchable keywords like 'Arduino' and 'sensor'
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Pata Chalta Hai?' videos about public-place gadgets (lift, mall door, tap, street light)
Near-duplicate topics such as repeated smoke detector, IR sensor and tap videos with the same question-style title
Reusing the same unchanged Hindi upload on YouTube expecting it to perform like Instagram
